practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran starter profile (12th NFL season, 76% snap share) — elevated Questionable active conversion (84%) & Wednesday maintenance tolerance.
factors: Did Not Participate (DNP) on Wednesday; remains sidelined from practice
practiceReport.beatComment: Hunter did not play in Thursday's win over the Colts due to his hamstring injury. The defensive end has still not returned to practice since sustaining the injury during Week 10 prep. If Hunter continues to miss practice, he will be in line to miss his third consecutive game due to the injury.

practiceReport.name: Kayshon Boutte
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (WR) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: This past Friday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston indicated that the hip injury Boutte suffered in last Thursday's win over the Colts didn't appear to be serious. However, with a DNP to start the practice week, the wideout's status will need to be monitored as Sunday's game against the Ravens approaches. Apart from a 4-125-2 receiving line in a 44-22 win over the Chargers in Week 9, Boutte has produced modest fantasy outputs more often than not, maxing out at five targets (three times) in 10 contests.

practiceReport.name: Sheldon Rankins
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Trench/box position (DT) — historically higher active rate through braced upper-body & ankle soreness (81% baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Rankins sustained an ankle injury during Thursday's win over the Colts and did not return to the contest. The defensive tackle's absence from Wednesday's session suggests the injury was significant. Rankins will have Thursday and Friday's sessions to return to practice in time to avoid an injury designation, or to at least have a chance to suit up for Sunday's game against the Ravens.

practiceReport.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (WR) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
factors: Returned to Limited Participation (LP) on Wednesday following 2-game absence
practiceReport.beatComment: Harrison has been sidelined for the Texans' last two contests, but the WR's ability to practice Wednesday, albeit in a limited fashion, bodes well for his chances of being available for Sunday's game against the Ravens. Harrison's fantasy impact in three outings with Houston since coming over in a trade with Arizona has been modest, so we'd like to see the No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft get a full and productive game in before endorsing him as a fantasy lineup option.

practiceReport.name: Keylan Rutledge
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (98% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
factors: Beat/podium consensus: on track to suit up
practiceReport.beatComment: The Texans announced Rutledge's injury in the waning moments of the contest, but he had been in the medical tent well before that time. Febechi Nwaiwu took over at left guard following Rutledge's departure. With Houston not set to play again until Sunday, Nov. 29, against Baltimore, Rutledge will look to recover from the stinger in time to suit up.

Coaching/beat trend (beat report): trending upward / optimistic to suit up
practiceReport.beatComment: Marks didn't practice last week before being ruled out for this past Thursday's 26-3 win over the Colts, but with some extra recovery time since then, the running back is trending toward a return to the lineup Sunday against the Ravens. To get there, however, he'll need to fully progress through the NFL's concussion protocol in the days leading up to the Texans' Week 12 contest.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Azeez Al-Shaair
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Al-Shaair was unable to play in Sunday's loss to the Browns due to a groin injury and personal matters. It had been unclear which issue contributed more to the middle linebacker's inability to practice in Week 10, but Monday's walkthrough provides further insight. Al-Shaair is clearly still suffering from the groin injury, and his status for the Texans' Thursday night showdown with the Colts remains uncertain.

irAndReserveTracker.name: British Brooks
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 8 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Brooks will miss at least four games. However, the 26-year-old has seen action only on special teams during the 2026 campaign, so his extended absence won't impact the usual day-to-day operations for the Texans offense.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Sam Hagen
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Hagen is an undrafted free agent out of South Dakota State. The reserve offensive lineman is 6-foot-6 and 320 pounds. The Texans clearly valued the rookie's training camp production, as the choice to keep the young player on the active roster will give him a chance to return to the 2026 season after at least four games on IR.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Ali Gaye
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: There's no designation to return attached to Gaye's placement on injured reserve, meaning the LSU product will be required to miss the entire 2026 season. He suffered a severe knee injury during the Texans' joint practice against the Panthers this past Wednesday. Gaye will shift his attention toward being fully healthy for the 2027 campaign.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Dylan Horton
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Horton's season is officially over after he tore his ACL during Monday's practice. The 25-year-old will now shift his focus to getting healthy for the 2027 campaign.

irAndReserveTracker.name: E.J. Speed
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Speed suffered a torn quadriceps tendon while lifting weights in May, and he underwent surgery to repair the injury. The linebacker is expected to miss the entirety of the 2026 season, and in his absence, Jake Hansen (ankle) and Henry To'oTo'o are set to operate as the team's primary outside linebackers.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Graham Mertz
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jayden Higgins
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jaylin Noel
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Noel was forced out of this past Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants after going down with the toe injury with just under nine minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. The loss of Noel is a major blow to the Texans, as he had been serving as the team's top return man in addition to emerging as a big-play threat on offense. Through Houston's first seven games, Noel had recorded 19 receptions for a team-leading 331 yards and two touchdowns and added 26 yards on four carries.

irAndReserveTracker.name: K.C. Ossai
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Ossai persisted through a separate issue to be activated off the active/PUP list for training camp in late July. The linebacker has unfortunately succumbed to yet another injury and could now miss the entirety of the 2026 regular season on the Texans' IR. Ossai will need to reach an injury settlement with the Texans if he wants to attempt a return to football with another team in 2026.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Mario Edwards Jr.
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Edwards suffered a torn ACL in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Colts and will miss the rest of the 2026 season. The defensive tackle has been moved to injured reserve and will no longer take up a spot on the Texans' 53-man roster.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Solomon Byrd
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Byrd suffered an ankle injury during last Friday's preseason finale against the Panthers. The defensive end had virtually no chance of making the 53-man roster, so he was waived with an injury designation. The 26-year-old went unclaimed and now will spend the entirety of the 2026 regular season on IR unless he is waived with an injury settlement.
